reasoning: Both sets fully specify all three stages, have detailed contracts, and include a 30-task M1 plan with context packets. B is stronger on RL: it has a tabular → DQN → CNN ladder with ablations, REINFORCE vs PPO as separate rungs, closed-form GAE, clipped-objective and Q-update golden cases, and careful handling of truncation versus termination. Its golden cases are also more concrete. A wins on the plan as a whole. Its pipelines are smaller and easier to read, and its milestone split follows dependency lines: one fish, then many fish, then local sight. Its M1 system task is small enough to build, and its thicken tasks are wired through stubs that the interface task creates. B puts each whole stage into a single very large milestone. Its framing has gone stale: the brief says 'Designing future environments now' is not being done, and S2 promises a 'deliberately revised' core even though M1 already builds the batch-first, team-based core. It also has a hidden dependency (M1-T26's CNN check needs M1-T27's network), and its final system task needs many hours of real 5-seed training across about 7 configurations while being sized S. A's main weaknesses are M2, which is a leftover-style 'replay + reference check + DQN thicken + write-up' milestone, an M1 that cannot yet show a replay, and a few stale fixture notes.
